chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Najiyah, from 'Amir ibn Kathir, from Abi al-Nuymir, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Verily, our Wilayah was presented to the inhabitants of the cities, but none accepted it as the people of Kufa did. And this is because the grave of Ali (peace be upon him) is in it, and close to it is another grave, meaning the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So, no one comes to it, prays two or four rak'ahs near it, and asks Allah for his need, except that Allah fulfills it for him. And verily, a thousand angels surround it every day.

key_terms.قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ (ع): The grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)
key_terms.قَبْرَ عَلِيٍّ (ع): The grave of Ali (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) in Kufa according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) identifies Kufa’s unique spiritual status as rooted in the proximity of Imam Ali’s (a.s.) grave to that of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), creating a dual sanctuary of Wilayah. This hadith underscores the theological principle that physical proximity to the Imams’ tombs facilitates divine acceptance of supplications, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding Ziyarat. The mention of a thousand angels daily encircling the grave highlights the continuous celestial witness and intercession associated with these sacred sites.
